referents.why: 'him' after 'you will say to him' is Pharaoh, the one Moses is sent to (masculine singular, addressee of the commanded speech).
'my people' is in the LORD's own words (thus says the LORD, cl3), so the first person is the LORD.
referents.category: first person inside quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' is in the LORD's own words, so 'me' is the LORD.
referents.category: first person inside quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'go' is an imperative the LORD gives to Moses (cl0), so its implied you is Moses.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the messenger

referents.why: 'you will say' is the second command in the same chain, addressed to Moses.
referents.category: implied subject of a command chain

referents.why: 'let go my people' is the innermost quoted command, spoken to Pharaoh, who is told to release them.
referents.category: implied you of a quoted command

referents.why: 'they may serve me' is third masculine plural; 'people' is a collective singular that takes plural agreement.
referents.category: plural agreement with a collective noun

links.why: A clause cannot follow itself; this is a builder self-link.
The weqatal 'you will say' continues the command 'go' (a weqatal continues what it follows).
The waw joins a command to a change of person (they serve me), which the and-rule reads as so that.
Let my people go, so that they may serve me: a third-person yiqtol after a command.
The LORD's words to Moses are the collection of commands go and say.
'You will say to him' introduces 'thus says the LORD', the nested speech.
'Thus says the LORD' introduces the command let go with its aim.

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses. Its part is the command collection; the commanded speech Moses gives to Pharaoh is nested as Exo.7.26#g1.
'Go' and 'tell' are commands joined by and at one level, so one imperative group with two command members. The builder's part role is not an imperative role.
Moses is commanded to say this; the words he speaks are his (R2), addressed to Pharaoh, and the quoted LORD turn is its part.
The innermost quoted speech of the LORD to Pharaoh. The conditional in Exo.7.27 continues the same quotation, so it is a part of this turn (R3).
Let go is the command; that they may serve me is its aim. The builder's part is not an imperative role.

none_fit.what: The imperative members (command, aim, basis, effect, warning) have no role for a speech that a command tells someone to make; the commanded speech is carried by a nested turn instead.
